title: Illustration Overview
slide_intent: Connect drawing style to what the brand wants people to notice while protecting the integrity of approved artwork.
strategic_value: Hand-drawn ingredients, a tall burger and a dripping ice cream can give Burger King a playful food vocabulary across packaging, stores and social media.
demonstration: A green explanatory column sits beside three labeled subjects: onion ingredients, an enlarged burger product and a hand holding soft serve on yellow and red.
practical_value: Choose among ingredient, product and storytelling illustrations, and follow the explicit limits on editing and extension.

content_islands.name: Style and use guidance
content_islands.spec: Place the description, use contexts and alteration limits in the left column.

content_islands.name: Ingredients
content_islands.spec: Use onion drawings in the adjoining green area under its label.

content_islands.name: Products and storytelling
content_islands.spec: Place the burger on yellow and hand-held soft serve on red in two tall panels.

ingredient.name: Storytelling illustration library
ingredient.role: Express food and playful human moments with a consistent hand-drawn voice.
ingredient.application: Use complete approved images without recoloring or cropping; make them big and bold where possible. Consult the Global Design Team for new simple illustrations or library expansion.
ingredient.scope: Historical 2020 partner guidelines, PDF produced January 2021. The overview artwork itself contains edge crops; retain the written no-cropping rule rather than deriving permission from this presentation.

reference_purposes.Intent: The copy describes the intended color, energy, humor and irony, focused on fresh ingredients, heroic products and playful storytelling.
reference_purposes.Expression: The three illustrated subjects demonstrate the hand-drawn style and color treatment.
reference_purposes.Application: The text names packaging, in-store artwork and social as use contexts.
reference_purposes.Constraint: Illustrations must not be recolored or cropped; use whole images, big and bold where possible, and consult the Global Design Team for new work or library expansion.
